APIErrorResponse.description: APIErrorResponse is the top-level envelope wrapping a ResponseError. All API error responses use this shape: { "error": { ... } }.

error.description: The error object containing details about what went wrong.

APIKey.description:
An API key used to authenticate requests to the Augno API.

A key always acts on behalf of the account it was created under, with the permissions of the role assigned to it.

name.description: Human-readable name for the API key.

redacted_value.description:
Redacted key value safe for display.

The key's prefix followed by its last four characters, e.g. `aug_sk_prod_****hjt4`.

role.description: Role assigned to the key, which determines the permissions of requests made with it.

last_used_at.description:
When the key was last used to authenticate a request.

Recorded at most once every 24 hours, so it can lag the key's most recent use by up to a day.

expires_at.description:
When the key expires and stops authenticating requests.

A key with no expiration keeps working until it is revoked or rotated.

revoked_at.description:
When the key's revocation takes effect.

A future timestamp means revocation was scheduled (for example, by a rotation) and the key continues to authenticate requests until that time.

Account.description:
An organization on Augno, including its branding and customer portal sub-resources.

Your own account and any customer or supplier account you trade with are both represented by this object.

name.description: The account's display name.

default_billing_address.description: The address billed by default on orders for this account.

default_shipping_address.description: The address shipped to by default on orders for this account.

branding.description: Customer-facing branding for the account, such as the logo, support contacts, and social links.

portal.description: The account's customer portal settings, including the portal URL slug.

AccountBranding.description: The customer-facing branding an account presents on its portal, emails, and documents.

support_email.description: The email address customers are directed to for support.

phone_number.description: The account's public contact phone number.

logo_url.description:
Stored location of the account's logo image.

Logos uploaded through the API are stored as an object key rather than a fetchable link, so use the Get Account Logo URL endpoint to obtain a short-lived download URL.

favicon_url.description:
Stored location of the account's customer-portal favicon.

Favicons uploaded through the API are stored as an object key rather than a fetchable link, so use the Get Account Favicon URL endpoint to obtain a short-lived download URL.

AccountGroup.description:
A named grouping of customer accounts, used for pricing rules or to categorize accounts.

A customer carries at most one group of type `type_group` as its customer type, plus any number of groups of type `pricing_group`. Membership of either kind can scope a volume discount to the customer and open up product lines for it to order from.

type.description:
How this account group is used.

- `pricing_group`: used for pricing rules, such as a "Preferred" group that receives a special discount.
- `type_group`: used to categorize accounts, such as "Consumers" or "Distributors".

A group's type is fixed when it is created and cannot be changed afterwards.

name.description:
Display name of the account group.

Unique within the account.

description.description: Free-form description of the account group.

commission_policy.description:
How sales commission applies to accounts in this group.

- `commission_applied`: sales commission is calculated on orders from accounts in this group.
- `commission_exempt`: orders from accounts in this group are exempt from commission.

freight_policy.description:
How freight charges apply to orders from accounts in this group.

- `free_freight`: customers within this group will not have to pay for freight.
- `billed_freight`: freight will be applied to any order within this account group, unless overridden elsewhere.

default_lead_time_days.description: Calendar days between an order being issued and it being due to ship, inherited by every customer in this group that has not set its own.

AccountIntegration.description:
Third-party integration connected to an account.

An account can have at most one integration per provider. The credentials supplied when the integration was connected are encrypted at rest and are never returned by the API.

name.description: Display name of the integration.

provider.description:
Integration provider code.

- `stripe`: Stripe payment processing.
- `shippo`: Shippo shipping and label generation.
- `hubspot`: HubSpot CRM.

status.description:
Lifecycle status of the integration.

Integrations are created `active`. Setting an integration to `inactive` keeps its stored credentials but stops it from being used (for example, the Stripe publishable key cannot be retrieved while the Stripe integration is inactive).

AccountPortal.description: The customer portal an account publishes for its customers to sign in to.

slug.description:
URL slug that identifies the account's customer portal.

Unique across all accounts.

AccountStatus.description:
A lookup value describing the standing of a customer account, such as whether shipments or all activity should be held.

The set of statuses is fixed by Augno and cannot be added to or edited; you apply one to a customer by setting the customer's `status`.

code.description:
Machine-readable status code.

- `normal`: standard account with no restrictions.
- `preferred`: account flagged for prioritized handling.
- `hold_shipment`: the account's shipments should be held, typically over a credit problem, while orders can still be placed.
- `hold_all`: all activity for the account should be held.

The hold statuses are advisory: they are surfaced as credit-hold warnings on the customer's orders, but they do not by themselves cause order or shipment requests to be rejected.

name.description: Human-readable label for the status.

owner.description:
Owner of this resource.

Account statuses are platform-provided and shared across all accounts, so the owner is always the Augno system owner.

AccountUser.description:
A user's membership in an account, carrying the account-specific status, role, and department.

Profile fields (name, email, username, image URL) live on the `user` sub-resource, which is shared across every account the user belongs to.

data.name: Packaging Line 1
data.notes: Initializes batches at the start of the packaging line.

data.name: CNC Router
data.notes: Spindle rebuilt March 2026; torque calibration due quarterly.

status.description:
The current state of this user's membership in the account.

- `active`: the user can sign in to the account and occupies one of the plan's seats.
- `disabled`: the user is locked out of the account and their sessions have been revoked, but the membership is retained.
- `removed`: the membership has been soft-deleted; it is hidden from listings by default and can be restored with the activate action.

role.description: The role that determines what this user is permitted to do in the account.

department.description: The department this user belongs to within the account.

data.name: Packaging Line 1
data.notes: Initializes batches at the start of the packaging line.

data.name: CNC Router
data.notes: Spindle rebuilt March 2026; torque calibration due quarterly.

user.description: The underlying user profile, shared across every account this person belongs to.

is_commission_eligible.description:
Whether this user can be assigned as a sales representative on orders, territories, and targets.

Independent of the `sales_rep` role type, which still scopes analytics and hides cost. Users with the `sales_rep` role are always eligible.

last_used_at.description: When the user last accessed this account.

created_at.description: When the account user was created.

updated_at.description: When the account user was last updated.

Actor.description: Reference to an actor — the user, API key, agent, or group identity associated with an action.

type.description:
Actor type.

- `user`: a human user account.
- `api_key`: a programmatic caller authenticating with an API key.
- `agent`: an automated agent acting on the account's behalf.
- `group`: a shared group identity, such as a "Customer Service" persona, rather than a single individual.

name.description: The actor's display name.

handle.description:
Human-readable handle identifying the actor.

- For `user` actors: the user's email address.
- For `api_key` actors: the redacted key value.

Other actor types carry no handle.

avatar_url.description:
URL of the actor's profile photo, if one is set.

Only populated for `user` actors.

role.description: The role the actor holds in the account, which determines what it is permitted to do.

AddConversationLinkRequest.description: Request to link a business record to a conversation.

resource_type.description: The kind of business record to link.

resource_id.description: The id of the business record to link.

AddMessagingGroupMemberRequest.description: Request to add a member to a reusable roster.

member_type.description: The kind of member being added, which decides whether `account_user_id` or `agent_config_id` is expected.

account_user_id.description: The account user to add (required when `member_type` is `user`).

agent_config_id.description: The agent to add (required when `member_type` is `agent`).

AddParticipantRequest.description: Request to add an account user to a group conversation.

role.description:
Role to grant the new participant.

- `admin`: can add and remove members and rename the conversation.
- `member`: can post, leave, mute, and react.
- `viewer`: read-only access.

`owner` is not accepted here; use the set-role endpoint to make an existing participant an owner.

Address.description: A saved address that can be used for billing and shipping on sales orders, invoices, and shipments.

name.description: Display name of the address.

phone.description: Phone number associated with the address.

email.description: Email address associated with the address.

type.description:
How the address is used.

- `standard`: a normal shipping or billing address.
- `drop_ship`: an address an order is shipped to directly, typically a third party or end customer rather than the account itself.

geolocation.description: Street-level location details for the address.

address_line_1.description: First line of the street address.

address_line_2.description: Second line of the street address.

AddressInput.description:
Address details supplied when creating an address, either on its own or inline on another resource.

A few requests, such as shipping rate estimates, take these same fields for a one-off address that is never saved to the account.

name.description: Display name of the address.

phone.description: Phone number associated with the address.

email.description: Email address associated with the address.

type.description:
How the address is used.

- `standard`: a normal shipping or billing address.
- `drop_ship`: an address an order is shipped to directly, typically a third party or end customer rather than the account itself.

street_line_1.description: First line of the street address.

street_line_2.description: Second line of the street address.

country.description: Two-letter ISO 3166-1 country code, such as `US`.

AddressSuggestion.description:
A candidate address returned by address autocomplete.

A suggestion is a lookup result from the address provider, not a saved address in your account. Creating an address from one is a separate step.

example.description: 123 Main St, Springfield, IL 62701, USA

id.description:
Identifier of the suggested place.

Pass this value as the `id` path parameter of the address details endpoint to retrieve the full parsed address. It is issued by the underlying address provider rather than by Augno, so it is not a durable Augno resource ID.

description.description: Full description of the address.

AdjustmentType.description:
A category of financial adjustment, such as a discount, fee, or write-off.

Adjustment types classify the `adjustment` transactions recorded against a customer.

name.description: Human-readable name of the adjustment type (e.g. "Discount").

code.description:
Machine-readable code identifying what kind of adjustment this is.

- `discount`: a price reduction.
- `shipping_discrepancy`: corrects a difference between quoted and actual freight.
- `short_payment`: reconciles an invoice paid for less than the amount due.
- `write_off`: cancels an uncollectible balance.
- `fee`: an additional charge.
- `refund`: returns money to the customer.

owner.description:
Owner of this resource.

Adjustment types are platform-provided and shared across all accounts, so the owner is always the Augno system owner.

AgentAction.description:
A single tool invocation performed by an agent during a run.

Each action records the tool that was called, its input and output, and any human review decision.

example.label: Read Doc
example.description: Read the Augno documentation page on creating sales orders.

tool.description:
The tool the agent invoked for this action.

- `create_artifact`: create an artifact such as a report, document, or data export.
- `read_doc`: read Augno documentation pages.
- `fetch_url`: fetch content from a public URL.
- `draft_reply`: propose a reply to the case's external party as a draft held for human approval (not sent).
- `send_email`: send an email reply through the conversation's bound inbox.

status.description:
Current action status.

- `pending_review`: awaiting human review before it can execute.
- `auto_approved`: automatically approved by policy.
- `approved`: manually approved by a user.
- `rejected`: rejected by a user; will not execute.
- `executed`: successfully executed.
- `failed`: errored during execution; see `error_message`.

label.description: Short human-readable label summarizing the action.

description.description: Longer description of what the action does.

run.description: Agent run this action belongs to.

input.description:
Arguments passed to the tool, as JSON.

Shape depends on `tool`. Encoded as a JSON value (object, array, string, number, boolean, or null), not a JSON-encoded string.

output.description:
Result returned by the tool, as JSON.

The shape depends on `tool`. An action that has not executed — because it is still waiting on a review decision, or was rejected — carries `{}`. Encoded as a JSON value (object, array, string, number, boolean, or null), not a JSON-encoded string.

error_message.description: Error message if the action failed.

entity.description: The resource this action operated on, when the tool targets a specific entity such as a customer or product.

review_requirement.description:
Whether a person must approve this action before it takes effect.

Fixed when the action is recorded, from the agent's review setting for that tool; tools that take an externally visible action, such as `send_email`, always require review and cannot be exempted. When review is required the action starts in `pending_review` and stays there until someone approves or rejects it; otherwise it is `auto_approved`.

reviewed_at.description: When a human review decision was recorded for the action.

updated_at.description: When this action was last updated.

AgentDefinition.description:
An AI agent available to the account.

The definition describes what the agent does, how its runs are triggered, the tools it can use, and whether it is currently enabled for the account.

example.name: Email Order Agent
example.description: Processes incoming emails and creates draft orders.

config.system_prompt: You are an order processing agent. Parse incoming emails and create draft orders.

tool.name: Lookup Customer
tool.description: Look up a customer by their email address.

definition_type.description:
Whether the agent is provided by Augno or created in this account.

- `system`: provided by Augno; cannot be edited or deleted.
- `custom`: created by a user in this account.

category_code.description: Category grouping for the agent (e.g. `order_processing`), used to organize agents in the UI.

trigger_type.description:
How runs of this agent are initiated.

- `scheduled`: runs on a cron schedule (see `config.trigger_config.cron_schedule`).
- `event`: runs in response to platform events (see `config.trigger_config.event_filters`).
- `manual`: runs only when explicitly invoked.
- `chat`: runs in response to a chat message; the run is linked to a conversation and posts its reply back into it.

name.description: Human-readable name of the agent.

slug.description:
URL-friendly identifier for the agent.

Unique within the account.

description.description: Description of what the agent does.

editability.description:
Whether this agent definition can be edited.

Always `read_only` for `system` definitions.

status.description:
Whether this agent is enabled for the current account.

Activation is per-account: a `system` agent shared across accounts can be `active` for one account and `inactive` for another. An `inactive` agent cannot be triggered.

role.description:
Role defining the permissions the agent operates with.

The agent acts as its own actor, and everything it does is authorized against this role — it can never reach data or actions the role does not grant. An agent with no role cannot execute: its runs fail immediately.

config.description: Agent-level configuration controlling LLM behavior and trigger settings.

example.system_prompt: You are an order processing agent. Parse incoming emails and create draft orders.

tool.name: Lookup Customer
tool.description: Look up a customer by their email address.

AgentDefinitionConfig.description:
Agent-level configuration controlling LLM behavior and trigger settings.

Distinct from per-tool configuration (`tools[].config`), which configures individual tools attached to the agent.

example.system_prompt: You are an order processing agent. Parse incoming emails and create draft orders.

system_prompt.description: Standing instructions that define the agent's role and how it should behave on every run.

tier.description:
Intelligence and cost tier for the agent's reasoning.

Selects how capable and expensive a model the agent uses without pinning a specific model; higher tiers reason better but cost more. Each tier resolves to an ordered chain of equivalent models, so a run automatically fails over to another provider's model if the preferred one is unavailable.

- `frontier`: the most capable tier, for multi-step planning, ambiguous agent work, and hard coding or architecture tasks.
- `high`: for normal planning, code edits, synthesis, and customer-facing reasoning.
- `balanced`: for research, summarization, classification, structured extraction, and light tool use.
- `cheap`: for simple transforms, validation, formatting, and routing.
- `legacy`: older-generation models kept for compatibility and regression comparison; avoid unless you specifically need them.

Leaving the tier unset picks one from how the agent is triggered: chat and manual runs use `high`, while scheduled and event-driven runs use `balanced` so background work stays cheap.

temperature.description:
LLM sampling temperature between 0 and 1.

Lower values make the agent's output more repeatable and literal; higher values make it more varied.

trigger_config.description:
Trigger-specific configuration.

Shape depends on the agent's `trigger_type`.

endpoint_tool_slugs.description:
API-endpoint tools the agent may discover and use, by slug (e.g. `create_account_group`).

These correspond to tools listed by the List Tools endpoint with category `api_endpoint`. A single entry `*` grants the entire endpoint-tool catalog.

endpoint_tool_review.description:
Per-endpoint-tool human-review overrides, keyed by tool slug.

When an entry is `true`, the run pauses in `awaiting_approval` each time the agent calls that endpoint-tool until it is approved via the Continue Agent Run endpoint. Slugs absent from the map do not require review.

AgentDefinitionTool.description:
Tool attached to an agent definition.

Pairs an AvailableTool with agent-specific config values.

tool.name: Lookup Customer
tool.description: Look up a customer by their email address.
Attached tool.

example.name: Lookup Customer
example.description: Look up a customer by their email address.

review_requirement.description:
Whether calls to this tool must be approved by a user before they execute.

When `required`, the run pauses in the `awaiting_approval` status each time the agent invokes this tool; approve or allow the tool via the Continue Agent Run endpoint to proceed. A tool whose `mutating` flag is true still pauses for approval even when this is `not_required`.

config.description:
Instance-specific configuration for this tool.

Must conform to the tool's `config_schema`. Encoded as a JSON value (object, array, string, number, boolean, or null), not a JSON-encoded string.

AgentMemory.description: A piece of information an agent has saved for recall in future runs.

example.content: Customer prefers express shipping for all orders.

category.description:
The kind of information this memory holds, used to group related memories.

- `preference`: how someone likes things done, such as a customer who always wants express shipping.
- `fact`: a durable detail worth remembering about the account or one of its records, such as a customer's typical order size.
- `instruction`: standing guidance for agents to follow, such as always confirming freight before issuing an order.

content.description: The information itself, written as plain text for an agent to read.

metadata.description: Arbitrary metadata as JSON. Encoded as a JSON value (object, array, string, number, boolean, or null), not a JSON-encoded string.

entity.description: The platform record this memory is about (e.g. a specific customer or product).

importance.description:
Relative importance from `0` to `1`, used to prioritize which memories the agent recalls.

An agent takes in only a limited number of memories per run, and the highest-importance ones are recalled first.

expires_at.description:
When this memory stops being used.

Past this time the memory is no longer recalled by agents and is omitted from list results, but it is not deleted and can still be retrieved by ID. A memory with no expiration is used indefinitely.

AgentRun.description: A single execution of an agent, from trigger through completion.

definition.name: Email Order Agent
definition.description: Processes incoming emails and creates draft orders.

config.system_prompt: You are an order processing agent. Parse incoming emails and create draft orders.

tool.name: Lookup Customer
tool.description: Look up a customer by their email address.

data.label: Read Doc
data.description: Read the Augno documentation page on creating sales orders.

trigger_type.description:
How this run was initiated.

- `scheduled`: started by the agent's cron schedule.
- `event`: started in response to a platform event.
- `manual`: started by an explicit request; see `triggered_by`.
- `chat`: started by a message in a conversation, with the agent's reply posted back into that conversation.

status.description:
Current run status.

- `pending`: queued but not yet started.
- `running`: currently executing.
- `awaiting_input`: paused, waiting for user input before continuing.
- `awaiting_approval`: paused, waiting for a pending action to be approved.
- `completed`: finished successfully.
- `failed`: stopped after an error; see `error_message`.
- `cancelled`: stopped before completion by a user.

definition.description: The agent definition this run executes.

example.name: Email Order Agent
example.description: Processes incoming emails and creates draft orders.

config.system_prompt: You are an order processing agent. Parse incoming emails and create draft orders.

tool.name: Lookup Customer
tool.description: Look up a customer by their email address.

input.description:
Input provided to the agent at the start of the run.

The shape depends on what started the run; a manually triggered run records `{"message": "<your input>"}`. Encoded as a JSON value (object, array, string, number, boolean, or null), not a JSON-encoded string.

output.description:
Final output produced by the agent.

Present once the agent has produced a result, including on a run that paused for more input or was cancelled part-way through. A run that has not produced one yet carries an empty object. Encoded as a JSON value (object, array, string, number, boolean, or null), not a JSON-encoded string.

error_message.description: Error message if the run failed.

triggered_by.description:
Actor that triggered this run.

Set only for runs started through the Trigger Agent Run endpoint; runs started by a schedule, a platform event, or a chat message have no triggering actor.

duration_ms.description: How long the run took, in milliseconds.

actions.description:
Tool invocations the agent made during this run.

Includes calls that were held for human review and never executed, so an entry here does not by itself mean the tool ran.

data.label: Read Doc
data.description: Read the Augno documentation page on creating sales orders.

steps.description:
Step-by-step timeline of what happened during the run.

Ordered by `sequence`, oldest first.

updated_at.description: When this run was last updated.

AgentRunStep.description: A single event in an agent run's execution timeline.

step_type.description:
The kind of timeline event.

Common values are `trigger_received`, `user_message`, `thinking`, `assistant_message`, `tool_call`, `tool_result`, `tool_blocked`, `awaiting_approval`, `completion`, and `error`. This is an open set — new step types are added as the agent runtime evolves, so treat unrecognized values as informational rather than failing on them.

content.description: Text payload for the step, such as a message body or a tool result.

sequence.description: Zero-based position of this step within the run's timeline.

duration_ms.description: How long this step took, in milliseconds.

metadata.description:
Additional structured data for the step.

The shape depends on `step_type` — for example a `tool_call` step carries the tool's arguments. Encoded as a JSON value (object, array, string, number, boolean, or null), not a JSON-encoded string.

AnalyzeDeliveryPerformanceRequest.description: AnalyzeDeliveryPerformanceRequest is the request to measure promises against shipments.

starts_at.description: The start date for the analysis period.

ends_at.description: The end date for the analysis period.

granularity.description: The period to break the results down by. Defaults to `week`.

AnalyzeDeliveryPerformanceResponse.description: How reliably promised delivery dates were met.

overall.description: The whole window as one figure.

periods.description: The same figures broken into periods, by the date each order was due.

backlog.description: Orders already past their promise and still unshipped, by how late they are.

uncommitted_order_count.description:
Issued orders in the window carrying no ship-by date, excluded from every rate above.

Reported so the exclusion is visible: a delivery score computed over half the order book, silently, is worse than one that says which half. A non-zero count here means orders placed before commitments were tracked still need a ship-by date.

AnalyzeOeeRequest.description: AnalyzeOeeRequest is the request to analyze Overall Equipment Effectiveness (OEE).

starts_at.description: The start date for the analysis period.

ends_at.description: The end date for the analysis period.

department_ids.description: Optional department IDs to filter by.

planned_time.description: Scheduled production time per department for the period. Availability, performance and OEE are only returned for departments this covers.

AnalyzeOeeResponse.description: AnalyzeOeeResponse represents the response from the analyze OEE endpoint.

AnalyzeOeeTrendRequest.description: AnalyzeOeeTrendRequest is the request to analyze Overall Equipment Effectiveness (OEE) over time.

starts_at.description: The start date for the analysis period.

ends_at.description: The end date for the analysis period.

department_ids.description: Restrict the analysis to these departments.

AnalyzeOeeTrendResponse.description: AnalyzeOeeTrendResponse represents the response from the OEE trend endpoint.

periods.description: One entry per production week in the requested window, oldest first.

AnalyzeScheduleAttainmentRequest.description: AnalyzeScheduleAttainmentRequest is the request to measure production against plan.

starts_at.description: The start date for the analysis period.

ends_at.description: The end date for the analysis period.

group_by.description: The dimension to break the results down by. Defaults to `week`.

machine_ids.description: Only measure production on these machines.

department_ids.description: Only measure production in these departments.

AnalyzeScheduleAttainmentResponse.description:
Actual production measured against the plan that was live at the time.

The baseline for each week is the version that was published on or before that week began, so republishing mid-horizon cannot rewrite a week the floor has already worked. `baseline_schedules` names the versions used, so any number here can be traced back to the plan that produced it.

group_by.description: The dimension the breakdown is grouped by.

baseline_schedules.description: The published versions the measurement was taken against.

baseline_status.description: Whether the period had a plan to measure against. When `no_baseline`, every ratio is null and the period has no plan rather than a missed one.

scheduled_machine_count.description:
Machines the plan asked for over this window.

Every figure in this response covers those machines only. Production scanned onto a machine no published version scheduled is excluded outright, so the score measures the plan that was made rather than the whole plant against it.

Announcement.description:
A broadcast announcement shown in the notification (bell) feed, carrying the calling user's own read state.

A single announcement is published to everyone in an account, or to every user on the platform, and each user keeps their own seen, read, and dismissed state for it. The status and timestamps you read are therefore always the caller's, and never reflect what anyone else has done with the same announcement. Notifications addressed to one user are a separate resource.

example.title: Scheduled maintenance
example.body: The platform will be briefly unavailable tonight at 2am UTC.

scope.description:
Who the announcement reaches.

- `account`: published to a single account and shown only to that account's users.
- `platform`: published by Augno and shown to every user across all accounts.

category.description:
The kind of event the announcement is about.

Announcements draw on the same categories as notifications, such as `system.broadcast` or `order.updated`, and the category is chosen by whoever publishes the announcement. The set is open-ended and may grow over time, so clients should tolerate values they do not recognize.

title.description: Short headline shown in the feed.

body.description: Supporting detail shown beneath the title.

status.description:
Where the announcement is in its lifecycle for the calling user.

- `unseen`: not yet surfaced to the caller.
- `seen`: surfaced in the caller's feed but not opened.
- `read`: explicitly opened by the caller.
- `dismissed`: removed from the caller's feed.

The status is derived from the caller's own seen, read, and dismissed timestamps and only ever moves forward, so the same announcement can show a different status for each user in the account.

priority.description: How prominently the announcement should be surfaced, from `low` through `urgent`.

resource.description: The resource the announcement is about, which the client can link to.

publish_at.description:
When the announcement becomes visible in the feed.

An announcement scheduled for the future is not returned by the announcement endpoints until this time passes.

expires_at.description:
When the announcement stops being shown.

Once it expires the announcement leaves every user's feed and can no longer be retrieved; an announcement with no expiry stays until each user dismisses it.

seen_at.description: When the calling user first saw the announcement.

read_at.description: When the calling user opened the announcement.

dismissed_at.description: When the calling user dismissed the announcement.

ApplyFulfillmentRecommendationsRequest.description: Request to adopt fulfillment recommendations for specific items.

item_ids.description:
Items whose recommendation should be adopted.

Named explicitly rather than applied wholesale: adopting advice in bulk without saying what is being adopted is how a plant changes what it builds by accident. Items not named here are left exactly as they are.

ApproveSendDraftRequest.description: Request to approve a customer-reply draft and send it to the customer.

client_message_id.description: A unique client-generated key for this approval, such as a UUID.

AssignConversationRequest.description:
Request to assign a customer-service case to a single owner — a user or a team.

The owner is a polymorphic (`assignee_resource_type`, `assignee_resource_id`) reference; omit both fields to clear the assignment.

assignee_resource_type.description:
What kind of owner the case is being assigned to.

- `account_user`: an individual teammate takes the case.
- `account_group`: a team takes the case, so anyone on it can pick it up.

assignee_resource_id.description:
The owner's id, an `account_user` or `account_group` matching `assignee_resource_type`.

Omit this and `assignee_resource_type` to clear the assignment.

AttachmentUploadTarget.description:
A presigned target for uploading a chat attachment directly to object storage.

PUT the file to `upload_url`, then send a message carrying an attachment whose `s3_key` is the key returned here. An upload that is never sent with a message is discarded automatically, so abandoning a target costs nothing.

attachment.description: A preview of the attachment the file becomes once it is sent with a message.

upload_url.description:
The presigned URL to PUT the file to.

Send the file with the same content type used to mint the target, or the upload is rejected.

s3_key.description:
The object-storage key identifying the uploaded file.

Pass it back as an attachment's `s3_key` when sending a message. It is bound to the conversation it was minted for and cannot be attached in another one.

expires_at.description:
When the upload URL stops working.

Targets are short-lived (about fifteen minutes); request a new one if the upload has not finished by then.

AttainmentBucket.description:
One row of a schedule-attainment breakdown.

Both ratios are reported because either alone misleads. `attainment_pct` caps each SKU at what was asked for, so over-building one easy item cannot paper over a total miss on another; `output_ratio_pct` does not cap, so it is the only one that reveals over-production.

key.description: Identifies the bucket within the chosen grouping — a week start, machine ID, department ID or item ID.

week_starts_at.description: First day of the week, when grouping by week.

planned_quantity.description: Units the live plan called for.

matched_quantity.description: Units produced that were planned for, capped per campaign at what was asked.

unplanned_quantity.description: Units produced with no matching planned campaign.

planned_run_hours.description: Machine hours the plan called for.

attainment_pct.description: Share of the plan that was met. Null when nothing was planned.

output_ratio_pct.description: Output as a share of plan, uncapped. Null when nothing was planned.

Attribute.description:
A selectable value within a property, such as `Red` for a `Color` property.

Attributes are assigned to items to classify them.

value.description: The selectable value this attribute represents, such as `Red` for a `Color` property or `Large` for a `Size` property.

color.description:
Swatch color used to display this attribute in the UI.

The named colors are arbitrary display choices; `default` is a neutral fallback used when no specific swatch applies.

sort_order.description:
Position of this attribute relative to its siblings within the property, starting at `1`.

Positions are kept contiguous: creating, reordering, or deleting an attribute automatically shifts its siblings.

property.description:
The property this attribute belongs to.

Populated only when the attribute is returned under an item's `attributes` list.

AuditEvent.description:
An immutable record of a single change to a resource, capturing who made the change, what changed, and when.

Audit events are recorded automatically as mutations happen; they cannot be created, edited, or deleted through the API. Recording is asynchronous, so an event may take a moment to become readable after the request that caused it has returned. An update that leaves every tracked field at its existing value records no event unless the mutation attaches metadata of its own — a password rotation, for example, records metadata and no field changes.

action.description:
The type of action this event records.

- `create`: the resource was created.
- `update`: one or more fields were changed.
- `delete`: the resource was deleted.
- `restore`: a previously deleted resource was restored.
- `archive`: the resource was archived.
- `approve`: a human approved a gated action, such as allowing a review-gated agent tool to run.
- `deny`: a human denied a gated action, such as rejecting a review-gated agent tool.

resource_type.description: Resource type of the audited entity.

account.description:
Account the audited mutation was performed against.

For a mutation on one of your own resources this is your account; when you act on a customer's or supplier's account, it is that account.

changes.description:
Field-level changes recorded for this event.

Only fields Augno tracks for that resource type are compared, and only those whose value actually differs are listed. Actions that do not alter stored fields, such as `approve` and `deny`, generally record no changes.

metadata.description: Arbitrary JSON metadata for the mutation (e.g. reason, source, tags). Encoded as a JSON value (object, array, string, number, boolean, or null), not a JSON-encoded string.

request.description:
Log of the API request that caused the mutation.

Changes that did not originate from an API request have no originating request log.

idempotency_key.description: Idempotency key of the originating request.

occurred_at.description:
When the audited mutation occurred.

Audit events are ordered and date-filtered by this timestamp rather than by `created_at`.

created_at.description:
When the audit event record was written.

Slightly later than `occurred_at`, since events are recorded out of band from the request that caused them.

AuditFieldChange.description: Field-level before/after transition recorded during a mutation.

field.description:
Name of the changed field.

Field names come from the audited record's stored representation and can differ slightly from the corresponding field on the API resource — for example `commission_policy_code` rather than `commission_policy`.

old_value.description:
Previous value as a JSON fragment.

`null` on `create` events, where the field had no prior value. Encoded as a JSON value (object, array, string, number, boolean, or null), not a JSON-encoded string.

new_value.description:
New value as a JSON fragment.

`null` on `delete` events, where the field has no remaining value. Encoded as a JSON value (object, array, string, number, boolean, or null), not a JSON-encoded string.

AvailableTool.description:
A capability an agent can be granted, allowing it to take that action during a run.

The catalog of available tools is the same for every account; granting one to an agent is what makes it callable.

example.name: Lookup Customer
example.description: Look up a customer by their email address.

slug.description: A stable identifier used when attaching the tool to an agent.

category.description:
Where the tool's behavior comes from.

- `built_in`: a capability implemented by the agent runtime itself, such as fetching a web page or drafting a reply for a teammate to approve.
- `api_endpoint`: an operation of this API exposed as a tool, letting the agent perform it on the account's behalf.

name.description: Human-readable name for the tool.

description.description:
Explanation of what the tool does.

This is also the description the agent's model reads when deciding whether to call the tool.

config_schema.description:
JSON schema describing the configuration options this tool accepts.

Defines the shape of the `config` field on AgentDefinitionTool: a schema declaring a `max_results` integer property means that tool's `config` may set `max_results`. Encoded as a JSON value (object, array, string, number, boolean, or null), not a JSON-encoded string.

required_permissions.description: Permission scopes the agent's role must hold for this tool to be usable (e.g. `products:read`).

required_role_type.description: Role type the caller must have for this tool, when the operation is gated by role rather than a permission (e.g. `admin`).

mutating.description:
Whether invoking this tool takes an action rather than only reading data.

True for any `api_endpoint` tool whose underlying operation is not a read, and for `built_in` tools that do something externally visible or hard to undo, such as sending an email. A mutating `built_in` tool always pauses its run for human approval and that gate cannot be turned off for an individual agent; for `api_endpoint` tools the flag is advisory and review stays configurable per agent.

BlockRequest.description: Request to block another account user from messaging the caller.

blocked_account_user_id.description:
The account user to block.

It must be someone else in your account; you cannot block yourself.

BulkDeleteSalesOrdersRequest.description: Request to bulk delete sales orders.

sales_order_ids.description: IDs of the sales orders to delete.

BulkUpsertItemCategoriesRequest.description: BulkUpsertItemCategoriesRequest is the request to bulk upsert item categories.

item_categories.description: Item categories to create or update, matched by name within the account.

BulkUpsertLocationsRequest.description: BulkUpsertLocationsRequest is the request to bulk upsert locations.

locations.description: Locations to create or update, matched by name within the account.

materials.description: Materials to create or update, matched by SKU within the account.

BulkUpsertPartsRequest.description: BulkUpsertPartsRequest is the request to bulk upsert parts.

parts.description: Parts to create or update, matched by SKU within the account.

BulkUpsertProductLinesRequest.description: BulkUpsertProductLinesRequest is the request to bulk upsert product lines.

product_lines.description: Product lines to create or update, matched by name within the account.

products.description: Products to create or update, matched by SKU within the account.

BulkUpsertPropertiesRequest.description: carries the properties to bulk upsert

properties.description: Properties to create or update, matched by name (case-insensitive) within the account.

BulkUpsertUnitGroupsRequest.description: BulkUpsertUnitGroupsRequest is the request to bulk upsert unit groups.

unit_groups.description: Unit groups to create or update, matched by name within the account.

BulkUpsertUnitsRequest.description: BulkUpsertUnitsRequest is the request to bulk upsert units.

units.description: Units to create or update, matched by name or abbreviation within the account.

Carrier.description:
A shipping carrier configured for fulfilling orders.

Carriers with a Shippo-supported `code` (`fedex`, `ups`, `usps`) are connected through Shippo for live rating and label purchase; other carriers represent self-managed shipping methods such as will call or local delivery.

name.description: Human-readable name for the carrier, unique among the carriers visible to your account.

code.description:
Well-known carrier identifier, set only for recognized carriers and absent for custom ones.

- `fedex`, `ups`, `usps`: integrated carriers managed through Shippo (live rating and labels).
- `will_call`: customer picks the order up; no carrier shipment.
- `delivery`: delivered by your own vehicles/drivers.
- `ltl`, `ltl1`: less-than-truckload freight carriers.
- `freight_collect`: freight billed to and arranged by the receiver.

account_number.description:
Your account number with this carrier.

UPS and USPS carrier accounts are connected to Shippo using this number; FedEx carriers authorize through OAuth instead, so their account number is not used to connect them.

customer_portal_visibility.description: Whether customers can see and select this carrier at checkout in the customer portal.

owner.description:
Provenance of this carrier.

System-owned carriers are platform-provided defaults shared across all accounts and cannot be updated or deleted; account-owned carriers are custom to your account.

service_levels.description:
Shipping service levels offered by this carrier (e.g. ground, overnight).

At most 10 service levels are returned inline; use the carrier's service levels endpoint to page through the full set.

CheckoutSalesOrderRequest.description: Request to create a checkout session for a sales order.

email.description: Email address to send the checkout link to.

checkout_url.description: URL of the hosted payment page where the customer completes the checkout.

ComputedRate.description:
A rate calculated on demand rather than stored.

The same shape as a rate minus the fields only a persisted row can have: it carries no ID and no timestamps because nothing was written. Used where a figure is derived per request, such as an analysis comparing one customer's price against the median other customers pay.

value.description:
Decimal value of the rate, as a string to preserve precision.

Expressed as the amount of the numerator unit per one denominator unit.

numerator_unit.description: Unit of the rate's numerator (e.g. the currency of a price).

denominator_unit.description: Unit of the rate's denominator (the per-unit basis, e.g. pairs for a price per pair).

example.system_prompt: You are an order processing agent. Parse incoming emails and create draft orders.

system_prompt.description:
Instructions that define the agent's role and how it should behave.

Sent to the model on every turn of a run, alongside the platform guidance Augno adds automatically.

tier.description:
Intelligence and cost tier for the agent's reasoning.

Selects how capable (and how expensive) a model the agent uses without pinning a specific model, so the agent keeps working as the underlying model catalog changes.

- `frontier`: the most capable and most expensive; multi-step planning, ambiguous work, tool-heavy workflows.
- `high`: normal planning, synthesis, and customer-facing reasoning.
- `balanced`: research, summarization, classification, structured extraction, and light tool use.
- `cheap`: simple transforms, validation, formatting, keyword lookup, and routing.
- `legacy`: older models kept for compatibility and regression comparison; avoid unless you specifically need them.

temperature.description:
How much randomness the model uses when generating text.

Lower values make the agent's output more repeatable; higher values make it more varied.

trigger_config.description:
Trigger-specific configuration.

Required contents depend on the agent's `trigger_type`; see the trigger config schema.

endpoint_tool_slugs.description:
API-endpoint tools the agent may discover and use, by slug (e.g. `create_account_group`).

These are the tools listed by the List Tools endpoint with category `api_endpoint`. The single entry `*` grants the entire endpoint-tool catalog. Omit or leave empty to grant none.

endpoint_tool_review.description:
Per-endpoint-tool human-review overrides, keyed by tool slug.

Set a slug to `true` to require human approval before the agent may execute that endpoint-tool; the run pauses in `awaiting_approval` until approved via the Continue Agent Run endpoint. Slugs omitted from the map do not require review.

Consumption.description:
Material consumed by a production step.

Each consumption records one input item and how much of it the step uses. Consumptions also determine the production flow: when another step produces the consumed item, the two steps are linked upstream/downstream automatically.

The quantities are stated against the step's own output, so a step producing 100 pairs and consuming 5 kg of yarn needs 5 kg per 100 pairs. Material requirements for an order scale every consumption in the flow by how much of the finished item is wanted.

category.name: Electronics
category.notes: Components and raw materials used across the electronics assembly line.

unit_group.name: Weight
unit_group.notes: Mass units used for ordering raw materials by weight.

quantity.description: Quantity of the material consumed by the production step.

waste_quantity.description:
Quantity of the material expected to be lost as waste.

Tracked separately from the consumed quantity, but added to it when material requirements are worked out, since the waste has to be bought as well.

consumed_item.description: The item consumed by the production step.

example.description: 6061-T6 aluminum sheet, 4ft x 8ft, 0.125in thick

category.name: Electronics
category.notes: Components and raw materials used across the electronics assembly line.

unit_group.name: Weight
unit_group.notes: Mass units used for ordering raw materials by weight.

instructions.description: Instructions for how this material is consumed.

ContactMatch.description:
A contact found by email on an account you have a relationship with — one of your customers, your suppliers, or your own account.

The same email can be a contact on many accounts across the platform; only accounts you relate to are returned.

Only active people are matched — someone who has been disabled or removed on an account never produces a match for that account.

data.name: Packaging Line 1
data.notes: Initializes batches at the start of the packaging line.

data.name: CNC Router
data.notes: Spindle rebuilt March 2026; torque calibration due quarterly.

id.description:
Contact match ID.

This is the matched account user's ID, so the same value also appears as `account_user.id`.

relationship.description:
How you relate to the account this contact belongs to.

- `customer`: the account is one of your customers.
- `supplier`: the account is one of your suppliers.
- `self`: the account is your own.

email.description: The email address that was matched.

data.name: Packaging Line 1
data.notes: Initializes batches at the start of the packaging line.

data.name: CNC Router
data.notes: Spindle rebuilt March 2026; torque calibration due quarterly.

account.description: The account this contact belongs to.

ContinueRunRequest.description: Request to resume a paused agent run.

example.message: Yes, proceed with creating the order.

message.description:
Message to send to the agent as the next turn of the run.

It accompanies any approval or denial in the same request, so use it to tell the agent how to proceed with what you just allowed or blocked.

approved_tool_slugs.description:
Slugs of tools whose pending calls should be approved.

Approves every call currently pending review for each named tool. Approval is one-time — the next call to the same tool pauses for review again. Tools you do not name are left pending, and the run resumes without them.

rejected_tool_slugs.description:
Slugs of tools whose pending calls should be denied.

The run keeps going: each denied call is answered with a "denied by user" result so the agent proceeds without it, instead of cancelling the run. A single resume may both approve and reject different tools.

approved_tool_call_ids.description:
Tool-call IDs (the `tool_use_id` of individual blocked calls) to approve.

Use this instead of `approved_tool_slugs` to approve ONE specific call when several pending calls share the same tool slug — approving by slug would approve all of them. Approvals are one-time.

rejected_tool_call_ids.description:
Tool-call IDs (the `tool_use_id` of individual blocked calls) to deny.

Per-call counterpart of `rejected_tool_slugs`, letting you deny one specific call among several that share a slug. Each denied call is answered with a "denied by user" result and the run continues.

Conversation.description: A conversation thread the caller participates in.

type.description:
What kind of conversation this is.

- `direct_message`: a 1:1 thread between two users.
- `group`: a named thread with multiple user or agent members (including customer-facing support cases).
- `system`: a system channel that delivers automated account alerts.

audience.description:
Whether this is a team-only conversation (`internal`) or a customer-facing case (`customer`).

A customer never sees an `internal` conversation, even one that is about them; within a `customer` case they see only the messages that were sent to them, not the team's internal notes on the case.

title.description:
The display title of a group conversation.

Direct messages carry no stored title; clients derive one from the participants.

workflow_status.description:
The triage lane of a customer-facing case.

Only conversations with a `customer` audience have a triage lane. It drives the support inbox and is independent of `status`, which is about visibility rather than progress.

- `new`: opened but not yet triaged.
- `open`: actively being worked.
- `waiting_internal`: blocked on the internal team.
- `waiting_external`: blocked on an external reply.
- `needs_approval`: a drafted reply is awaiting human approval.
- `resolved`: closed out.

group.description:
The reusable roster this conversation was started from.

This is provenance only: the roster's members were copied into the conversation when it was created, so later edits to the roster never add or remove participants here, and deleting the roster only clears this reference.

status.description:
The conversation's state from the caller's point of view.

- `active`: a normal, visible conversation.
- `archived`: archived for the whole account.
- `hidden`: the caller dismissed the conversation from their own list while everyone else still sees it, which takes precedence over an account-level archive.

legal_hold.description:
Whether the conversation is under legal hold.

While held, the conversation is exempt from automatic retention purging and from redaction until the hold is released.

assignee.description: The owner of the case: either a `user` actor (an individual team member) or a `group` actor (a team).

participants.description:
The participants of the conversation.

Only current members are listed; anyone who left or was removed is omitted, even though their past messages remain in the thread.

topic.description:
The app record this conversation is anchored to, such as a sales order.

Anchored conversations surface as the discussion thread on that record.

unread.description: Number of messages the caller has not yet read.

last_message_at.description: When the most recent message was sent.

last_message.description: The most recent message in the conversation.

example.body: Sounds good — shipping it today.

ConversationLink.description:
A reference from a conversation to a business record it concerns, such as an order, invoice, shipment, or customer.

Links sit alongside the conversation's primary `topic` anchor, so one thread can reference several records. Listing conversations by business record matches the topic anchor and these links alike, which is what surfaces a conversation on the record's own page.

conversation.description: The conversation this link belongs to.

type.description:
The kind of participant.

- `user`: an account user (a teammate).
- `agent`: an AI agent.
- `system`: the system itself, which posts automated messages.
- `customer`: an external customer in a support case.

role.description:
The participant's permission level in the conversation.

- `owner`: can rename or delete the conversation and manage its members and their roles.
- `admin`: can add or remove members and rename the conversation.
- `member`: can post, react, mute, and leave.
- `viewer`: read-only access.

membership.description:
The participant's membership in the conversation.

- `active`: currently a member.
- `left`: voluntarily left the conversation.
- `removed`: removed by an admin.
- `hidden`: still a member but has hidden the conversation from their own list.

Membership records are kept rather than deleted, so re-adding someone who left or was removed reactivates their original record and their earlier messages stay attributed to them.

notifications.description:
The participant's notification preference for the conversation.

- `unmuted`: receives notifications for new messages.
- `muted`: new-message notifications are suppressed, though a direct @mention still raises an in-app alert (never an email), and the conversation still counts toward the unread total.

actor.description:
The user or agent behind this participant.

A customer participant resolves to the `user` actor of the person who opened the case; the `system` participant that posts automated messages has no actor.

agent_trigger_policy.description:
For agent participants, when the agent is invoked in response to messages.

- `mention`: only when the agent is @mentioned.
- `keyword`: when a message contains one of the agent's trigger keywords.
- `always`: on every human message in the conversation.

agent_trigger_keywords.description:
For agent participants with a keyword or mention policy, the keywords that trigger it.

Matching is case-insensitive and looks anywhere in the message body: under `keyword` the bare word is matched, under `mention` it must appear as `@keyword`. Replying directly to one of the agent's own messages always reaches it, so an agent with no keywords still answers replies but nothing else.

read_cursor.description: The participant's read position in the conversation (read receipts): how far they have read.

CreateAPIKeyRequest.description: Request to create an API key.

role_id.description:
ID of the role to assign to the API key.

The role determines what requests authenticated with the key are allowed to do. A key keeps its role for life — including through rotation — so issue a new key to use a different one, while changes to the role's own permissions take effect for existing keys immediately.

name.description:
Human-readable name for the API key.

Shown when listing keys and used to match keys when searching, so prefer something that identifies the integration using it.

expires_at.description:
When the key expires and stops authenticating requests.

If omitted, the key keeps working until it is revoked or rotated.

CreateAccountGroupRequest.description: Request to create an account group.

example.name: Wholesale Customers
example.description: Customers who buy in bulk at wholesale pricing.

name.description:
Display name of the account group.

Must be unique within your account.

type.description:
How this account group will be used.

- `pricing_group`: used for pricing rules, such as a "Preferred" group that receives a special discount.
- `type_group`: used to categorize accounts, such as "Consumers" or "Distributors".

The type cannot be changed after creation.

commission_policy.description:
How sales commission applies to accounts in this group.

- `commission_applied`: sales commission is calculated on orders from accounts in this group.
- `commission_exempt`: orders from accounts in this group are exempt from commission.

Leave this out and the group is created commission-exempt, so orders from its accounts earn no sales commission until you change it.

freight_policy.description:
How freight charges apply to orders from accounts in this group.

- `free_freight`: customers within this group will not have to pay for freight.
- `billed_freight`: freight will be applied to any order within this account group, unless overridden elsewhere.

default_lead_time_days.description: Calendar days between an order being issued and it being due to ship, inherited by every customer in this group that has not set its own.

description.description: Free-form description of the account group.

CreateAccountIntegrationRequest.description: Request to create or upsert an account integration.

name.description: Display name of the integration.

provider.description:
Integration provider code.

- `stripe`: Stripe payment processing.
- `shippo`: Shippo shipping and label generation.
- `hubspot`: HubSpot CRM.

credentials.description:
JSON string containing the provider's credentials.

Required keys depend on the provider:

- `stripe`: `private_key` (`sk_...`), `publishable_key` (`pk_...`), and `webhook_secret` (`whsec_...`).
- `shippo`: `api_key` (`shippo_live_...` or `shippo_test_...`).
- `hubspot`: `access_token` (`pat-...`).

For Stripe and Shippo, sandbox accounts must supply test keys and production accounts must supply live keys; credentials that do not match are rejected. HubSpot tokens make no such distinction.

CreateAccountUserRequest.description: Request to create an account user.

name.description: User display name.

email.description:
User email address.

Either `email` or `username` must be provided. If a user with this email already exists, that user is added to the account instead of a new user being created, and the request fails with a conflict if they are already an active member of it.

username.description:
Unique username.

3–255 characters; letters, numbers, underscores, and hyphens. Either `email` or `username` must be provided. Providing a username without an email creates a scanning station user.

password.description:
Password for scanning station users.

Required when creating a scanning station user (username without email) and rejected for all other users, who instead receive a generated password in their welcome email. Must be 8–72 characters and include an uppercase letter, a lowercase letter, a number, and a special character.

role_id.description:
ID of the role to assign to the user.

The role you supply can be overridden: users added to a customer account always receive the shared customer role so their portal capabilities stay permission-driven, and scanning station users in any other account receive the scanner role. Supplying a role whose type is `sales_rep` normalizes to the account's canonical sales-rep role.

department_id.description:
ID of the department to assign to the user.

The department must already exist in the account you are acting in.

is_commission_eligible.description:
Whether the user can be assigned as a sales representative on orders, territories, and targets.

Defaults to false. Forced true for the `sales_rep` role type and rejected for scanner and agent roles.

preferences.description:
Notification preference toggles for the new user.

Only applies when creating a user in another account you manage (cross-account); ignored when creating a user in your own account.

CreateAgentRequest.description: Request to create an agent definition.

example.name: Inventory Monitor
example.description: Monitors inventory levels and creates restock alerts.

config.system_prompt: You are an order processing agent. Parse incoming emails and create draft orders.

name.description: Human-readable name of the agent.

slug.description:
URL-friendly identifier for the agent.

Must be unique within your account.

description.description: Description of what the agent does.

category_code.description: Category grouping for the agent (e.g. `order_processing`), used to organize agents in the UI.

trigger_type.description:
How runs of this agent are initiated.

- `scheduled`: runs on a cron schedule; `config.trigger_config.cron_schedule` is required.
- `event`: runs in response to platform events; at least one `config.trigger_config.event_filters` entry is required.
- `manual`: runs only when explicitly invoked.
- `chat`: runs when a user messages the agent in a conversation, and the agent's reply is posted back into that conversation.

Whatever the trigger type, a run can always be started by hand with the Trigger Agent Run endpoint.

config.description: Agent-level configuration controlling LLM behavior and trigger settings.

example.system_prompt: You are an order processing agent. Parse incoming emails and create draft orders.

tools.description: Built-in tools to attach to the agent.

role_id.description:
ID of the role that defines the permissions the agent operates with.

Every API call the agent makes is authorized against this role, so it bounds what the agent can see and change. An agent created without a role cannot execute — its runs fail immediately — so attach one before triggering it.

CreateAttachmentUploadURLRequest.description: Request to mint a presigned upload target for a chat attachment.

filename.description: The original filename of the file to upload.

content_type.description:
The MIME content type of the file.

The file must then be uploaded with this same content type, or object storage rejects it. It also decides how the attachment preview returned here is classified: `image/…` becomes an inline image, anything else a file.

value.description:
The selectable value this attribute represents, such as `Red`.

Must be unique across all attributes in the account, not just within the property. Leading and trailing whitespace is trimmed.

color.description:
Swatch color used to display this attribute in the UI.

When omitted, one of the nine named colors (everything except `default`) is assigned at random.

sort_order.description:
Position of the new attribute relative to its siblings within the property, starting at `1`.

Must be at most the property's current attribute count plus one; siblings at or after this position are shifted one position later. Defaults to the last position if not provided.

name.description:
Human-readable name for the carrier.

Must not match another carrier already visible to your account, including the system-provided ones.

code.description:
Well-known carrier code.

Providing a Shippo-supported code (`fedex`, `ups`, `usps`) connects the carrier through Shippo and syncs its service levels; the other codes, such as `will_call` and `delivery`, simply describe a self-managed shipping method. Omit the code entirely when none of them fit. The code cannot be changed after the carrier is created.

account_number.description:
Your account number with this carrier.

Required when `code` is `ups` or `usps`, whose carrier accounts are connected to Shippo using this number; FedEx authorizes through OAuth instead, so no account number is needed.

customer_portal_visibility.description: Whether customers can see and select this carrier at checkout in the customer portal.

type.description:
The kind of conversation to create.

- `direct_message`: a 1:1 thread with exactly one other user. Addressing yourself is allowed and gives you a private notes thread.
- `group`: a named thread with any number of user and agent members.

`system` channels are created by the platform and cannot be requested here.

participant_account_user_ids.description:
The other participants to add.

For a direct message, exactly one account user. For a group, the members to seed — these can be omitted when `group_id` supplies a roster, or when the conversation is anchored to a topic resource, since a record discussion may start solo and pull people in later.

The caller is always a participant and does not need to be listed; on a group they become its owner and every other member seeded at creation is notified.

group_id.description:
Seed a group conversation from a reusable roster.

The roster's current members are copied into this conversation (in addition to any `participant_account_user_ids`); the conversation is independent afterward. Ignored for direct messages.

title.description:
Title for a group conversation.

A direct message is identified by its participants rather than by a title.

topic_resource_type.description:
The type of business record to anchor this conversation to.

An anchored conversation is returned when conversations are listed for that record, which is how a discussion shows up on an order or invoice.

topic_resource_id.description: The id of the business record to anchor this conversation to.

name.description: The customer's business name, as shown throughout the app and on documents.

number.description:
Human-readable customer number used to identify the account, distinct from the `id`.

Must be unique within your account. If omitted, the next sequential number is assigned automatically.

status.description:
The customer's account standing.

- `normal`: standard account with no restrictions.
- `preferred`: account flagged for prioritized handling.
- `hold_shipment`: the customer's shipments should be held, typically over a credit problem, while orders can still be placed.
- `hold_all`: all activity for the customer should be held.

edi_status.description: Whether EDI (Electronic Data Interchange) is enabled for exchanging orders and documents with this customer.

commission_policy.description:
How sales commission applies to this customer's orders.

- `commission_exempt`: this customer's orders are exempt from sales commission.
- `commission_applied`: sales commission is calculated on this customer's orders.

freight_policy.description:
Whether this customer is billed for freight on their orders.

- `free_freight`: the customer is not billed for freight.
- `billed_freight`: freight is billed to the customer.

Freight is also waived when the customer's type group, one of its price groups, or a product line the ordered products belong to is `free_freight`.

lead_time_days.description:
Calendar days between an order being issued and it being due to ship.

Sets each order's `ship_by_date` when it is issued. Leave unset to inherit the customer's account group lead time, then the account default.

default_carrier_id.description: ID of the carrier used on this customer's orders when the order does not specify one.

default_service_level_id.description: ID of the carrier service level used when an order takes its carrier from this customer's default.

default_payment_term_id.description: ID of the payment term used on this customer's orders when the order does not specify one.

default_shipping_term_id.description: ID of the shipping term used on this customer's orders when the order does not specify one.

default_priority.description: Priority used to pre-fill new orders for this customer.

default_sales_rep_id.description:
The ID of the account user to credit as the sales rep on this customer's orders.

Must be an account user on your own account.

customer_price_group_ids.description: IDs of the account groups of type `pricing_group` to assign to this customer, used to apply pricing rules.

customer_type_group_id.description: ID of the account group of type `type_group` that categorizes this customer (for example "Distributors").

carrier_billing_type.description:
Who pays the carrier for shipments.

- `sender`: the shipper (you) pays the carrier.
- `third_party`: a third party is billed, using `carrier_billing_account`.

carrier_billing_account.description: Carrier billing account number charged when `carrier_billing_type` is `third_party`.

credit_limit.description: Maximum credit extended to this customer.

bill_to_address.description: Default billing address, created along with the customer.

ship_to_address.description:
Default shipping address, created along with the customer.

If identical to `bill_to_address`, a single shared address record is created.

CreateDemandOverrideRequest.description: Request to create a demand override.

scope_type.description:
What the override targets.

- `item`: a single item.
- `product_line`: every item sold under one product line.
- `account`: every item in the plan, which is how a blanket assumption such as "plan for double demand" is expressed.

scope_ref_id.description:
ID of the item or product line the override targets.

Omit it for an `account`-wide override, which targets every planned item rather than one thing. The ID is checked against the account's items and product lines, so an override cannot be created against something that does not exist.

period_starts_at.description:
First day of the demand period the override applies to.

Overrides are applied month by month, so every calendar month the period touches is adjusted and any time of day is ignored.

period_ends_at.description:
Last day of the demand period the override applies to.

Must fall on or after `period_starts_at`.

adjustment.description:
How the value adjusts the forecast.

- `absolute`: replaces the forecast for each month in the period.
- `delta_units`: adds the value to each month in the period.
- `delta_percent`: scales each month in the period by the value as a percentage.

When several overrides land on the same month they are applied in that order, so a percentage always acts on the already-adjusted number.

value.description:
The amount of the adjustment, interpreted according to `adjustment`.

A `delta_percent` value is a number of percent, so `-25` plans a quarter less than the forecast; it cannot go below `-100`. An `absolute` value cannot be negative, while a `delta_units` value can, so that a cancelled program removes demand.

unit_id.description:
ID of the unit the value is expressed in.

Recorded for context only: the value is applied to the planned demand without unit conversion, so a unit adjustment should be stated in the unit the item is planned in.

reason.description:
Why the adjustment was made.

The reason is carried into each schedule the override changes, so a plan can explain why a month departs from history.

note.description:
Free-form notes about the adjustment.

This is the text the free-text search on the list endpoint matches against.

effective_at.description:
When the override starts being applied to newly generated schedules.

When omitted, the override starts applying straight away.

expires_at.description:
When the override stops being applied to newly generated schedules.

When omitted, the override keeps applying until it is deactivated or deleted.

active.description:
Whether the override is taken into account when a schedule is generated.

Send `false` to stage an adjustment that should not affect schedules yet; an override is otherwise created ready to apply.

name.description:
Display name of the department.

Must be unique within your account; maximum 255 characters.

location_id.description: ID of the location where this department operates.

scanning_station_ids.description:
IDs of scanning stations to assign to this department.

A scanning station belongs to one department at a time, so listed stations are moved out of their current department.

machine_ids.description:
IDs of machines to assign to this department.

A machine belongs to one department at a time, so listed machines are moved out of their current department.

labor_rate.description:
Hourly labor rate for work done in this department, such as a changeover technician.

Production scheduling costs changeovers with the constraint department's rate when one is set, falling back to the account-wide changeover labor rate setting. The numerator unit must be a currency and the denominator must not be.

CreateEmailDomainRequest.description: Request to register a sending/receiving domain with the email bridge.

domain.description:
The fully-qualified domain name to register (e.g. `support.acme.com`).

Supply a bare domain, not an email address; the value is lowercased before it is stored.

CreateEmailInboxRequest.description: Request to provision a routable inbox on a verified domain.

email_domain_id.description: The verified domain this inbox belongs to.

address.description:
The full inbox address (e.g. `support@acme.com`).

Its domain part must match the selected domain, which must already be verified. The address is lowercased before it is stored, and it must not already be in use by another inbox.

from_name.description: Display name for the `From` header of outbound mail.

agent_config_id.description:
The agent to bind to this inbox to handle incoming mail.

With no agent bound, mail is still threaded into a conversation for your team, but nothing runs on it automatically.

agent_trigger_policy.description:
How the bound agent decides whether to run on incoming mail.

- `mention`: runs only when the agent is @mentioned, matched against the trigger keywords below.
- `keyword`: runs when the message contains any of the trigger keywords.
- `always`: runs on every incoming message.

Leaving this unset makes the agent run on every incoming message, since email has no reliable @mention convention.

agent_trigger_keywords.description:
The keywords that decide whether the agent runs on an incoming message.

Under the `keyword` policy a keyword matches anywhere in the message; under `mention` it only counts where it is prefixed with `@`.

group_id.description:
The messaging group (roster) whose members are seated on every conversation this inbox opens.

Must name a group in your own account. Agents in the group are seated to run only when @mentioned, so they do not all fire alongside the inbox's own agent.

CreateItemCategoryRequest.description: Request to create an item category.

name.description: Display name of the item category.

type.description:
What kind of items this category groups.

- `material_category`: groups raw materials and components (items of type `material`).
- `product_category`: groups finished products and parts (items of type `product` or `part`).

The type is fixed once the category is created.

unit_group_id.description:
ID of the unit group that determines the units of measure available to items in this category.

Must be one of your account's unit groups or a platform-provided one. After creation the unit group can only be replaced by another unit group of the same unit type, through the Change Item Category Unit Group endpoint.

name.description:
Display name of the location.

Maximum 255 characters.

type.description:
This location's level in the storage hierarchy.

The levels run from largest to smallest: `building`, `section`, `aisle`, `rack`, `shelf`, `bin`. They are descriptive labels rather than a rule — the parent you choose is not required to be the next level up.

parent_id.description:
The location this one sits under in the storage hierarchy.

Must be an existing location in your account. Omit to create a top-level location.

child_ids.description:
Existing locations to attach beneath the new location.

Each listed location is reparented onto the new location, detaching it from its current parent. Every ID must belong to your account.
